items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the bishop on g6 can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop on g6 can go to exactly these squares.

hints: A bishop moves along diagonals and may capture.
Two diagonals pass through g6; the squares on them are free until a piece blocks.
Seven squares: c2, d3, e4, f5, f7, h5 and h7.
items.explain: The bishop on g6 slides along the diagonal h7-g6-f5-e4-d3-c2 and along the diagonal h5-g6-f7. It can capture the pawn on c2 and it may go to e4, d3 or h5, but some of those squares are attacked at once. The three quiet choices are f5, h7 and f7.

items.prompt: Does the black bishop guard the pawn on e6 in this position?

claims.statement: After ...Bf7 one black piece guards e6.
The bishop stands on f7.

hints: Which squares does the bishop on f7 attack?
Look at the diagonal down to the left.
Yes: f7 attacks e6.
items.explain: The bishop on f7 attacks the adjacent diagonal square e6, so it guards the pawn.

items.prompt: Does the black bishop guard the pawn on e6 in this position?

claims.statement: After ...Bh7 no black piece guards e6.
The bishop stands on h7.

hints: Which diagonal does the bishop on h7 stand on?
It looks along g6 and f5, away from e6.
No: nothing guards e6.
items.explain: The bishop on h7 looks down the long diagonal towards b1, which does not pass e6, and no other black piece reaches e6. The pawn stands alone.

items.prompt: Does the black bishop guard the pawn on e6 in this position?

Does the pawn on a6 look at e6?
Yes: the bishop guards e6, and the a-pawn is far away.
items.explain: The bishop on f7 still guards e6, and the a-pawn move has nothing to do with it. Only the bishop's square matters for this question: the pawn move on the a-file is the irrelevant change.

items.prompt: White to move. The bishop on f5 guards e6 and the pawn on d4 looks safe. Find the engine's first choice at depth 16.

claims.statement: 9.g4 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
9.Bd3 is at least 120 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
9.Qh5+ is at least 150 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
9.Bc4 is at least 40 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which white piece can attack the bishop and gain space at the same time?
A pawn attacks without being traded for a bishop easily.
The pawn from g2 goes to g4.
items.explain: The pawn on g4 attacks the bishop, which must leave f5, and the bishop's squares are few. The bishop to d3 blocks the queen's guard of the pawn on d4, so Black's queen takes it. The queen check on h5 runs into the pawn move to g6, and the bishop to c4 is a little slower than the pawn. Engine, depth 16: the pawn move leads.

feedback_by_move.f1d3: The bishop blocks the d-file, so nothing guards d4 and the black queen takes it.
feedback_by_move.d1h5: A check, but ...g6 attacks the queen and Black is far ahead; the next board shows the trap behind it.
feedback_by_move.f1c4: A good developing move but about two-thirds of a pawn behind the pawn thrust.

items.prompt: Black to move. Can the bishop take the pawn on g4 and win a pawn safely?

claims.statement: After 9.g4 two white pieces (the queen on d1 and the knight on e5) guard the pawn on g4.
Taking on g4 loses the bishop for a pawn in the engine's main line.

hints: Who guards the pawn on g4?
The queen on d1 sees g4 along the diagonal, and the knight on e5 attacks it too.
No: a white piece retakes the bishop.
items.explain: The queen on d1 looks along the diagonal e2, f3, g4 and the knight on e5 also attacks g4, so the pawn is guarded twice. After the bishop takes, a white piece retakes and Black has swapped a bishop for a pawn, giving up the extra piece the whole line was built on.

items.prompt: Black to move, in check from the queen. Two blocks are possible. Which one survives?

claims.statement: Blocking with the g-pawn is the engine's top move (depth 16).
Blocking with the bishop is at least 800 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at what stands behind the block on g6.
If the bishop blocks, the queen can capture it with check.
The pawn on g7 goes to g6.
items.explain: The bishop on g6 would be taken by the queen, and the king on e8 has no escape square, so that is mate. The pawn on g6 blocks and attacks the queen, which must retreat. Engine, depth 16: the pawn block is the top move; the bishop block loses at once.

feedback_by_move.f5g6: Qxg6 is checkmate: the king has no square and nothing can take the queen.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's bishop attacks e6. How many black pieces guard that pawn right now?

claims.statement: After 8...Bh7 9.Bc4 no black piece guards e6.
After 8...Bh7 9.Bc4 one white piece attacks e6.

hints: Check each black piece: which of them attacks e6?
The bishop on h7 looks the other way along its diagonal.
None: the pawn is unguarded.
items.explain: No black piece attacks e6: the bishop on h7 looks along the b1-h7 diagonal, the queen on d8 and the knights do not reach e6, and the pawn on f7 is gone. White's bishop on c4 attacks it, so Black must find a guard or accept losing a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move, a knight up. White's bishop attacks yours. One natural queen move loses at once. Find the engine's first choice at depth 16.

claims.statement: Developing with ...Nf6 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
9...Qd5 is at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The bishop on h7 is guarded once, by the rook.
A queen move to d5 opens the d-file but leaves the king in the open.
The knight goes to f6.
items.explain: After ...Qd5 White checks on h5 and the king must go to d8; then the knight jumps to f7 with check on the king and an attack on the rook. After ...Kd7 the queen takes on d5 with check, so Black loses the queen to the other queen. Developing the knight keeps the trade on h7 harmless: the rook can retake. Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is first; ...Qd5 is at least three pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.d8d5: Qh5+ Kd8 Nf7+ forks the king and the rook, and after ...Kd7 the queen takes the queen on d5 with check.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Bc4. Two natural moves, a knight move and a pawn move, lose material. Find the developing move that works.

claims.statement: 9...Nf6 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
9...Nd7 is at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
9...b5 is at least 500 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Two natural moves, a knight move and a pawn move, both lose material.
The move that works develops a piece without blocking the queen or leaving f7 short.
The knight from g8 goes to f6.
items.explain: The knight on f6 develops, covers d5 and leaves the queen's diagonal alone. The knight on d7 blocks the queen and the pawn thrust to b5 takes a tempo that Black cannot afford: both lose a piece or more to the bishop on e6. Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is first by a wide margin.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: After Nxf7 Kxf7 Qg4 the pawn on e6 falls with check.
feedback_by_move.b7b5: Bxe6 and Black loses material: taking back runs into Qh5+ and a mate.

items.prompt: White to move, a knight down. Which queen move adds a second defender to the knight on e5?

claims.statement: After 10.Qe2 two white pieces (the queen and the d4 pawn) defend the knight on e5.
After 10.Qd3 one white piece (the d4 pawn) defends the knight on e5.
After 10.O-O one white piece (the d4 pawn) defends the knight on e5.

hints: The knight on e5 is defended once, by the d4 pawn.
Which queen move puts the queen on the e-file, behind the knight?
The queen goes to e2.
items.explain: From e2 the queen stands behind the knight on the e-file and defends it. When the knight jumps to f7, the queen attacks e6 along the file, and the bishop on c4 attacks it as well. Qd3 is also a main move, but it does not stand behind the knight, and castling adds no defender. The engine's first choice between Qe2 and Qd3 changes with depth.

feedback_by_move.d1d3: Also a main move, but it adds no second defender to the knight on e5.
feedback_by_move.e1g1: Natural, but it adds no defender to the knight and spends a move.

items.prompt: Black to move after 10.Bxe6. Two white pieces attack the bishop on f7, but the bishop can simply take the attacker on e6. What happens after 10...Bxe6?

answer.class: White mates in three, starting with Qh5+
options: Black is a piece up and safe
White mates in three, starting with Qh5+
White wins the queen with Nxf7

claims.statement: After 10.Bxe6 two white pieces attack the bishop on f7.
After 10...Bxe6 White mates in three with 11.Qh5+.

hints: If the bishop leaves f7, what stops the queen from using the h5-e8 diagonal?
After ...Bxe6 look at the squares h5, g6 and f7.
Qh5+ g6, Qxg6+ Bf7, Qxf7#: mate.
items.explain: Counting two attackers against one guard shows the pressure, but it hides a capture: the bishop on f7 can take the attacker on e6. That capture removes the bishop from the h5-e8 diagonal, and Qh5+ g6 Qxg6+ Bf7 Qxf7# mates. Before you capture, ask what the capturing piece used to guard.

On h7 it looks along the other diagonal and leaves the pawn alone, so a white bishop on c4 attacks a pawn nobody guards. Engine, depth 20: ...Bf7 leaves White the best number of the three, ...Bf5 the worst.
